spans.s: Śaurpa-ṇāyya, ‘descendant of Śūrpaṇāya,’ is the patronymic of a teacher, a pupil of gautama, in the first two Vaṃśas (lists of teachers) in the Mādhyaṃdina recension of the Bṛhadāraṇyaka upaniṣad (ii. 5, 20; iv. 5, 26).

Saurī is given by Zimmer as the name of an unknown animal at the aśvamedha (‘horse sacrifice’) in the taittirīya Saṃhitā. But this is an error: saurī means ‘dedicated to the sun.’
Foot notes Altindisches Leben, 99.
